```{r}
# Librerías
library(ordinalNet)
library(openxlsx)
library(caret)

# Leer los datos
data <- openxlsx::read.xlsx("datos_PCA.xlsx")

# Variable respuesta
y <- factor(data$X1ª_eval, levels = c("RP", "EE", "PE"), ordered = TRUE)

# Matriz de predictores
data_predictoras <- data[, !(colnames(data) %in% c("Mejor_resp", "X1ª_eval"))]
data_predictoras[] <- lapply(data_predictoras, function(x) {
  if (is.character(x)) as.factor(x) else x
})
X <- model.matrix(~ . -1, data = data_predictoras)
```

# GRID ORDINALNET

```{r}
# Valores de alpha a explorar
alpha_list <- c(0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1)

# Lista para guardar resultados
results <- data.frame()

# Bucle para ajustar un modelo con cada valor de alpha
for (a in alpha_list) {
  fit <- ordinalNet(
    x = X, y = y,
    family = "cumulative", link = "logit",
    alpha = a,
    parallelTerms = TRUE, nonparallelTerms = FALSE,
    standardize = TRUE
  )
  
  # Extraer la mejor lambda según el mínimo AIC
  best_idx <- which.min(fit$aic)
  
  results <- rbind(
    results,
    data.frame(
      alpha = a,
      lambda_opt = fit$lambdaVals[best_idx],
      devPct = fit$devPct[best_idx],
      AIC = fit$aic[best_idx],
      BIC = fit$bic[best_idx]
    )
  )
}

# Ver resultados
print(results)
```

# OrdinalNetCV (mejor alfa y lambda)

```{r}
library(ordinalNet)
library(caret)

set.seed(123)

n <- nrow(X)

library(writexl)

# Convertir a data frame
X_df <- as.data.frame(X)

# Exportar a Excel
write_xlsx(X_df, path = "variables-ordinalNET-X1eval.xlsx")


preds <- character(n)

# Validación Leave-One-Out manual con alpha y lambda óptimos
for (i in 1:n) {
  train_idx <- setdiff(1:n, i)

  model <- ordinalNet(
    x = X[train_idx, ],
    y = y[train_idx],
    alpha = 1,
    lambdaVals = 0.00244,
    family = "cumulative",
    link = "logit",
    parallelTerms = TRUE,
    nonparallelTerms = FALSE,
    standardize = TRUE
  )

  # Convertir el índice predicho a etiqueta del factor
  pred_index <- predict(model, newx = X[i, , drop = FALSE], type = "class")
  preds[i] <- levels(y)[as.integer(pred_index)]
}

# Convertir a factor con niveles correctos
preds <- factor(preds, levels = levels(y), ordered = is.ordered(y))
length(preds)
# Evaluar con matriz de confusión
confusionMatrix(preds, y)



```


```{r}
length(preds)
```



```{r}
# Coeficientes del modelo (excluyendo interceptos)
coefs <- coef(model)
coefs <- coefs[!grepl("Intercept", names(coefs))]

# Ordenar variables activas por valor absoluto del coeficiente
coefs_ordenados <- sort(abs(coefs[coefs != 0]), decreasing = TRUE)

# Mostrar los nombres ordenados
variables_ordenadas <- names(coefs_ordenados)
```

```{r}

top_n <- 34  # Cambia esto según lo que necesites
variables_top <- variables_ordenadas[1:min(top_n, length(variables_ordenadas))]

# Subconjunto de X solo con las variables activas
X_filtrado <- X[, variables_top, drop = FALSE]

library(caret)

set.seed(123)
n <- nrow(X_filtrado)
preds <- character(n)

for (i in 1:n) {
  train_idx <- setdiff(1:n, i)

  model <- ordinalNet(
    x = X_filtrado[train_idx, ],
    y = y[train_idx],
    alpha = 1,
    lambdaVals = 0.00244,
    family = "cumulative",
    link = "logit",
    parallelTerms = TRUE,
    nonparallelTerms = FALSE,
    standardize = TRUE
  )

  pred_index <- predict(model, newx = X_filtrado[i, , drop = FALSE], type = "class")
  preds[i] <- levels(y)[as.integer(pred_index)]
}

# Convertir a factor con los niveles correctos
preds <- factor(preds, levels = levels(y), ordered = is.ordered(y))

# Matriz de confusión
confusionMatrix(preds, y)
```





# 0.647

```{r}
# Librerías
library(ordinalNet)
library(openxlsx)
library(caret)

# Leer los datos
data <- openxlsx::read.xlsx("datos_PCA.xlsx")

# Variable respuesta
y <- factor(data$Mejor_resp, levels = c("RC", "RP", "EE", "PE"), ordered = TRUE)

# Matriz de predictores
data_predictoras <- data[, !(colnames(data) %in% c("Mejor_resp", "X1ª_eval"))]
data_predictoras[] <- lapply(data_predictoras, function(x) {
  if (is.character(x)) as.factor(x) else x
})
X <- model.matrix(~ . -1, data = data_predictoras)

# Variables seleccionadas (de la iteración 8)
mejores_vars <- c(
  "Leukocytes_slope", "Smoking_exposure", "Platelets_cv", 
  "SII_diff_2C_1eval", "Platelets_media", "Lymphocytes_cv", 
  "PCR", "PLR_slope", "SII_diff_1C_2C", "Platelets_diff_2C_1eval"
)

X_mejores <- X[, mejores_vars, drop = FALSE]

# LOO
pred_loo <- vector("character", length = nrow(X_mejores))
for (i in 1:nrow(X_mejores)) {
  X_train <- X_mejores[-i, , drop = FALSE]
  y_train <- y[-i]
  X_test  <- X_mejores[i, , drop = FALSE]

  modelo_i <- ordinalNet(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    family = "cumulative",
    link = "logit",
    parallelTerms = TRUE,
    nonparallelTerms = FALSE,
    alpha = 1
  )

  pred <- predict(modelo_i, newx = X_test, type = "class")
  pred_loo[i] <- if (is.null(pred)) NA else as.character(pred)
}

# Evaluación
niveles_ordenados <- levels(y)
pred_loo_factor <- factor(pred_loo, levels = 1:4, labels = niveles_ordenados, ordered = TRUE)
confusionMatrix(pred_loo_factor, y)
```
